texts.preamble: Shakeel(Dar) vs Rajesh Ram(403/22Nfc) on 9 May, 2024 :1: In The Court Of Ms. Charu Gupta Presiding Officer, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-01 (Se), Saket Courts : New Delhi Mact No.: 542/24 Mohd. Shakeel v. Rajesh Ram Cnr No.: Dlse01-000355-2023 Mohd. Shakeel S/o Mohd. Kalu Khan R/o Jhuggi Near Out Gate of Okhla Mandi, New Delhi. And also R/o: Ps Bahadurgarh, Distt-Hapur U.P. .....Petitioner/claimant Versus 1.Rajesh Ram S/o Sh. Upinder Ram R/o K-68, Salam Roti Wali Gali Okhla Head, Jamia Nagar New Delhi. ............Driver/ Respondent no. 1 2. Sanjay @ Sanju Ram S/o Sh. Lalan Ram R/o H.No.4, Jasola Village Sarita Vihar, New Delhi ............. Owner/ Respondent no.2 Date of accident : 25.10.2022 Date of filing of Dar : 15.03.2023 Date of Decision : 09.05.2024 Mact No: 542/24 Mohd. Shakeel v. Rajesh Ram P.No. 1 Of 18 Bk Award 1.
texts.facts: The present accident claim is based on a detailed accident report (DAR) filed by the police in terms of provisions of MV Act. 2. As per the investigation by the police officials, on 25.10.2022 at about 10.15 AM, injured Mohd. Shakeel alongwith his relative were going towards Jamia via Modi Mill Flyover. As they get down from the flyover before Masihgarh Chowk, one TSR came at a very rash and negligent manner from Kalkaji Mandir side and hit injured from behind and got injured. Said TSR also got turned turtle and driver of said TSR bearing No. DL-1RZ7726 (hereinafter referred to as offending vehicle) also received injuries. Name of said TSR driver was revealed as Rajesh Ram. Relative of injured/Mohd. Shakeel took him to AIIMS hospital alongwith driver of TSR in Ambulance. Shakeel(Dar) vs Rajesh Ram(403/22Nfc) on 9 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/61905449/ 1 3. An FIR no. 0403/22 dated 25.10.2022 was registered u/s 279,337 of IPC at PS New Friends Colony and the matter was investigated. MLC of injured was obtained. After investigation a charge sheet was filed before Ld. MM. 4. Respondent no.1 and 2 appeared initially but thereafter stopped appearing. Further, no Reply/Written statements were filed on behalf of Respondent no.1 and 2. Vide order dated 10.04.2023, respondent no.1 and 2 were directed to furnish security of Rs.1,50,000/- as the offending vehicle was uninsured at the time of accident. In compliance of such order, Respondents deposited FDR for Rs.1 lac only. 5. After completion of pleadings, following issues were framed on 04.08.2023. MACT NO: 542/24 Mohd. Shakeel v. Rajesh Ram P.No. 2 Of 18 BK 1. OPP. 3. Relief. 6. Thereafter, PW-1 Mohd. Shakeel led his evidence by way of affidavit as Ex.PW1/A and relied upon copy of Aadhar card as Ex.PW-1/1(OSR), copy of PAN card as Ex.PW-1/2(OSR), copy of MLC as Ex.PW-1/3(part of DAR), copy of discharge summary & OPD cards as Ex.PW-1/4, original medical bills as Ex.PW-1/5 and DAR as Ex.PW-1/6(colly). He was not cross- examined by Respondents. 7. Respondents did not lead any evidence. In the present case, petitioner/injured has specifically deposed that on 25.10.2022 at about 10.00 AM, he was going towards Batla House from Okhla Mandi by keeping fruits on his Rehri. When he reached at Modi Flyover, NFC, New Delhi, suddenly a TSR bearing no. DL1RZ7726 came at a very rash and negligent manner and hit him from behind forcefully and sustained grievous injuries in his pelvic and all over the body. He was taken to AIIMS hospital. Thereafter, he got treatment from Family Health Hospital Meerut, U.P. where he was operated and plates were also implanted. He deposed that he was doing work of selling fruits on Rehri at Batla House Market and earning Rs.25,000/- p.m. He deposed that he had spent more than Rs.3,00,000/- towards his treatment/special diet, conveyance and other expenses. He was not cross-examined by any of the respondents. 11. From the evidence so recorded which was unrebutted, it is apparent that the accident was caused due to sole negligence on the part of the driver of offending vehicle and liability to compensate the victim. Further, MLC Ex.PW-1/3 reflects that the injured suffered abrasion over right knee, right elbow, left hand and over scalp. As per Ex.PW-1/4(colly), medical record of Family Health hospital also reveals that the injured suffered fracture of right inferior and superior pubic rami and of anterior wall and anterior MACT NO: 542/24 Mohd. Shakeel v. Rajesh Ram P.No. 4 Of 18 BK coulmn of right acetablum. Thus, the injury sustained by the petitioner is proved to be grievous in nature. 12. In the present case, police after investigation had filed charge sheet against Respondent no.1 under Section 279/338 of IPC which is also suggestive of negligence of respondent in causing the accident. The IO has filed Detailed Accident Report before this Tribunal. 13. No respondent witness entered into the witness box to oppose the case of injured/petitioner. Accordingly, issue no.1 is decided in favour of petitioner/ claimant/applicant and against the respondents.
texts.arguments: Reliance is placed upon decision in Bimla Devi & ors. vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & ors. (2009) 13 SC 535, in Parmeshwari vs. Amir Chand & ors., 2011 (1) SCR MACT NO: 542/24 Mohd. Shakeel v. Rajesh Ram P.No. 3 Of 18 BK 1096 and National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pushpa Rana, 2009 ACJ 287, wherein it has been held that the negligence has to be decided on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities and a holistic view has to be taken. In National Insurance Co. vs. Pushpa Rana 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi, it was laid down that completion of investigation and filing of charge sheet are sufficient proof of negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle. As regards the quantum of compensation, this court is governed by the law laid down by Hon'le Supreme Court in Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 Supreme Court cases 343, Sarla Verma & Ors. v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Ors. (2003) 6SCC 121 and National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi & Ors.(2017) 16 SCC 680. The gist of the law is that the object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. 18.6. It was observed by Hon'ble Sc in such case of Raj Kumar (supra) that what usually poses some difficulty is the assessment of the loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability--Item (ii) (a). 18.7. The State Bank of India, Saket Courts, Delhi is directed to disburse the amount in accordance with MACAD Shakeel(Dar) vs Rajesh Ram(403/22Nfc) on 9 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/61905449/ 8 formulated by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi. 28. At this stage, it is relevant to the refer to the judgment of A. V. Padma & Ors. Vs., R. Venugopal & Ors. (2012) 3 Supreme Court Cases 378: " ......In the case of Susamma Thomas (supra), this Court issued certain guidelines in order to "safeguard the feed from being frittered away by the beneficiaries due to ignorance, illiteracy and susceptibility to exploitation". But if the Tribunal is satisfied for reasons to be stated in writing that the whole or part of the amount is required for expanding an existing business or for purchasing some property for earning a livelihood, MACT NO: 542/24 Mohd. Shakeel v. Rajesh Ram P.No. 14 Of 18 BK the Tribunal can release the whole or part of the amount of compensation to the claimant provided the Tribunal will ensure that the amount is invested for the purpose for which it is demanded and paid. However, the Tribunals are often taking a very rigid stand and are mechanically Shakeel(Dar) vs Rajesh Ram(403/22Nfc) on 9 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/61905449/ 9 ordering in almost all cases that the amount of compensation shall be invested in long term fixed deposit. Hence a change of attitude and approach on the part of the Tribunals is necessary in the MACT NO: 542/24 Mohd. Shakeel v. Rajesh Ram P.No. 16 Of 18 BK interest of justice..."
